context.objective: Document how this process works, including controls and what remains unresolved.

turns.text: The process is an in-kind distribution of securities. The client can elect one, but execution is on operational hold because our controlling 7.8.3 checklist and 7.8.4 tax guidance are unavailable.
When a client elects a distribution in kind, what steps are established before the operational hold, if any?

The client gives written direction. The designed procedure documents authority and conditions, timing, eligible lots and adviser instructions before valuation and allocation. GPFS coordinates, client counsel owns legal conclusions and the client tax adviser owns tax conclusions. The missing checklist and guidance block execution, even if there is a client election.
What does the designed procedure say happens after valuation and allocation, before securities are transferred?

Under the documented design, allocation is provisional until final pricing and client approval. Whole shares go to investors and a fractional remainder stays open with no default rounding. Counsel and the investment bank clear the legal package in writing. Investor Services issues client-approved notices via FA-01. The transfer agent or custodian tracks delivery per investor; no live execution is authorized now.
In the documented design, what marks the DIK as complete after the transfer agent or custodian tracks delivery?

Every investor delivery must be confirmed or explicitly open; share/value and fractional remainders must reconcile before completion. Accounting updates the GL, non-cash proceeds, capital accounts, carry and cost/basis. We keep approvals, checklist and preparer/reviewer sign-off in the binder. The internal approver, storage details and role titles remain unconfirmed. This is the designed closeout, not a completed event.
What, if anything, changes for the client or investors while execution is on hold?

The practical effect is we must not send instructions or deliver securities while the operational hold is in force. The write-up doesn't describe what the client or investors actually did while waiting, or how long it lasted. A client election alone does not satisfy the missing legal, tax and controlled-checklist requirements.
What concrete consequence could result from executing a DIK incorrectly, or from the hold continuing?

An incorrect lot can irreversibly change basis and holding period. Missing securities clearance blocks release; insecure transfer of tax identifiers is a confidentiality risk. I don't know the financial impact of a longer hold. I can't confirm any workaround, elapsed time or executed event from the source.
Under the documented design, what happens to a fractional remainder that remains open after the distribution?
